steps: Verify the provider-issued SPF and DKIM records and review the DMARC policy covering the visible From domain.
Configure a monitored DMARC reporting address and an appropriate policy with the DNS admin; do not weaken an existing enforced policy blindly.
Send a controlled test and inspect original headers. Confirm DMARC passes using aligned SPF or DKIM.
Fix failures before production sends and retain header evidence.
10.ascii:
Visible From domain
       |
       +--> SPF identity + alignment
       +--> DKIM identity + alignment
                       |
                       v
             DMARC pass + reporting

steps: Select an approved From name and authenticated From address; verify the address is supported by the configured domain.
Set the Reply-To to a monitored mailbox and assign who responds to incoming questions.
Check campaign and workflow sender settings so defaults do not override the intended identity unexpectedly.
Send a test, reply to it and verify both receipt and the appearance/function of tracked links.
11.ascii:
Campaign / workflow
       |
       v
Approved From --> recipient
                     |
                     v
Reply-To mailbox --> assigned responder

steps: Back up the GHL audience or preserve an approved source export before cleanup.
Compare HubSpot migration records with GHL email identities, opt-in evidence, exclusions and original contact source.
Resolve missing or conflicting suppression data. Keep uncertain records outside the sending audience until reconciled.
Record the actual historical-audience count. Permission already exists according to the brief; this task verifies it was retained during migration.
14.ascii:
HubSpot migration evidence --> GHL audit
                     |
                     +--> Opt-in / source retained
                     +--> Suppression retained
                     +--> Gaps --> hold / resolve

steps: Select the eligible audience, use LC Email validation or the existing verification process.
Run validation and review valid, invalid and uncertain outcomes; validation does not establish consent.
Deduplicate by normalized email, preserving useful history and the most restrictive suppression state.
Quarantine invalid and uncertain addresses and reconcile the resulting count against the original list.
16.ascii:
Eligible records
       |
       v
Validation + duplicate review
       |
       +--> Approved valid unique records
       +--> Invalid / uncertain --> quarantine

steps: Identify existing email DND, unsubscribe, complaint and hard-bounce states in the account.
Apply the supported email suppression controls and create an explicit exclusion rule for marketing audiences.
Check that imports, tags and workflow enrollment cannot silently reactivate opted-out contacts.
Use controlled test contacts to verify that campaigns and workflows both exclude suppressed recipients; record actual behavior.
17.ascii:
Unsubscribe / complaint / hard bounce
                  |
                  v
          Email suppression / DND
                  |
                  v
      Excluded from campaigns + workflows

steps: In Contacts, create an eligible historical-audience Smart List with valid email and email suppression exclusions.

Create an engaged pilot list using recent clicks, responses or other relevant customer activity. Reported historical responses are only 30–110 out of 8,000; permission alone does not make all 8,000 engaged.
For event invitations, exclude confirmed registrants for the specific event using a reconciled import or working sync.
Inspect sample contacts and counts. Keep event registration separate from future-marketing permission.
18.ascii:
Historical audience --> valid + not suppressed
                               |
                               +--> Engaged pilot
                               +--> Full invitation list
Exclude confirmed registrants for this event

steps: In Marketing > Email, create a reusable Market Better invitation template.
Set the configured From/Reply-To, subject, event details and the intended Eventbrite/Contrast registration link.
Add personalization with safe fallbacks, postal address and the supported unsubscribe element.
Save and preview desktop/mobile. GHL sends invitations; Contrast sends confirmations and reminders to registered attendees.
21.ascii:
Sender + event details + brand
             |
             v
GHL invitation template --> registration link
             |
             v
Preview + personalization test

steps: Add GHL’s supported unsubscribe element to every marketing template and confirm it is visible and usable.
Send a controlled test and inspect received headers for List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click support.
Use the body opt-out and the mailbox’s one-click route where available; confirm requests update email suppression.
Verify no later marketing reaches that test contact. A body link alone does not replace the required one-click headers.
22.ascii:
Marketing message
  +--> Body opt-out link
  +--> One-click unsubscribe headers
                    |
                    v
          Suppression --> no later marketing

steps: Create controlled test contacts representing normal recipients, missing personalization data and opted-out recipients.
Send tests and inspect desktop/mobile layout, sender identity, headers and all links.
Unsubscribe a test contact and attempt a later small campaign/workflow test; verify suppression without exposing real contacts.
Record pass/fail results and screenshots or message references; fix failures before signing off.
24.ascii:
Test contact matrix
  +--> Normal recipient --> correct layout / links
  +--> Missing name ----> safe fallback
  +--> Unsubscribed ---> excluded
                 |
                 v
             QA evidence

steps: Open Marketing > Email > Campaigns and create a test campaign for controlled recipients only.
Choose Send / Schedule > Batch Schedule; configure a small test quantity, repeat interval, active days and timezone.
Verify recipients and observed batch timestamps. Keep the production list out of this configuration test.
Save a final-cadence preset of 250 every 15 minutes, but use it at full scale only after the warm-up and capacity checks.
25.ascii:
Controlled test audience
          |
          v
Batch Schedule: quantity + interval + timezone
          |
          v
Observed timing / recipient count / stop test

steps: Inspect supported Eventbrite, Contrast and GHL integrations, exports, APIs or webhooks available in the actual accounts. Select and cost a verified route.
Map normalized email/names, original/latest source, marketing permission, event ID, external registration ID and status/time; confirm registration in Contrast before marking it confirmed in GHL.

Implement contact upsert and duplicate-event protection. Many attendees are new; check existing identities first, retain the event source, preserve opt-outs and do not grant future-marketing consent from event registration alone.
Add an integration log, retries/reconciliation and error ownership. Test both new Eventbrite leads and existing GHL contacts; a controlled import can be an interim route only with documented latency.
26.ascii:
Eventbrite --> verified transfer --> Contrast
                                       |
                                       v
                           Confirmed registration
                                       |
                                       v
Sync / reconciled import --> match normalized email
       + existing --> update contact + event
       + new ------> create contact + event
Failure --> log / retry / reconciliation

steps: Use the confirmed registration update for a stable event ID to drive GHL’s registration marker or equivalent event-history record.
Stop or skip invitation follow-ups for that event while preserving eligibility for future shows when permission allows.
Keep confirmation, join-link and attendee reminders in Contrast; disable any conflicting GHL workflow messages for this purpose.
Test both new and existing registrants, including someone registered for an earlier show, and verify no duplicate email handoff occurs.
27.ascii:
Contrast confirms event X registration
                   |
                   v
GHL event X status --> stop invitations X
                   |
                   +--> Future event Y: re-evaluate
Contrast sends attendee confirmations / reminders

steps: Before each GHL invitation or follow-up, recheck marketing permission, suppression and recipient frequency.
Check confirmed registration for this specific event, not a permanent registered flag left from an earlier event.
Check registration-sync freshness and unresolved errors; hold follow-ups and reconcile when the data cannot be trusted.
Test registration or unsubscribe during a workflow wait. Ensure the next GHL invitation is skipped while Contrast owns attendee reminders.
28.ascii:
Before GHL invitation X
        |
        v
Permission + not suppressed + fresh event data?
        + NO --> hold / skip
        + YES --> registered for event X?
                    + YES --> skip invitation
                    + NO ---> send if frequency allows

steps: Build controlled cases for a new Eventbrite lead, an existing migrated GHL contact and a contact already unsubscribed from marketing.
Replay the same registration update, register someone for two shows and simulate a delayed or failed sync; use test mechanisms supported by the chosen route.
Verify one contact per identity, event-specific status and source attribution, preserved permission/suppression and no automatic marketing reactivation for new Eventbrite/Contrast attendees.
Confirm Contrast owns attendee reminders and GHL same-event follow-ups stop. Test retry/reconciliation and document counts, timestamps and remaining exceptions.
29.ascii:
Test cases --> registration sync
 + new / existing --> create OR update
 + replay ---------> no duplicate
 + prior opt-out --> suppression retained
 + event X / Y ----> separate event states
 + failure --------> recover / reconcile
                     |
                     v
No duplicate attendee reminders

steps: Create a send log containing campaign ID, segment, time, recipient count, sent count and current account allowance.
Record invited, delivered, clicked, responded, registered and attended separately. Confirm the definition of response and keep the 30–110 historical estimate separate from measured results.
Verify Google Postmaster Tools access where possible; record its Gmail signals separately from GHL metrics.

Match event attendance to existing/new GHL contacts and event source. About 60%–75% of 250 attendees are reportedly new; do not attribute them all to GHL email. Record missing or delayed data explicitly.
30.ascii:
GHL campaign results + Gmail signals
                   |
                   v
           Send log / monitoring
                   |
                   v
           Continue / slow / pause

steps: Use the operating thresholds below and identify the operator who will pause campaign batches and related workflow sends.
On a controlled scheduled campaign, use Marketing > Email > Campaigns > actions menu to test Pause and confirm its state.
Test stopping related workflow sends separately; document messages already queued or delivered and the restart procedure.
Record that Resume after the original scheduled time can send immediately. Recheck audience and capacity before any restart; Cancel cannot be resumed.
31.ascii:
Warning / stop signal
          |
          +--> Pause future campaign batches
          +--> Stop related workflow sends
          |
          v
Fix --> smaller test --> explicit restart review

steps: Select the engaged pilot list and a small starting volume appropriate to account history and live limits.
Recheck funding, sender authentication, suppression and the tested template; schedule the pilot.
Monitor headers, failures, bounces, deferrals and feedback; review delayed engagement/complaint reports when available.
Record the outcome and fix or hold on failures before increasing volume.
33.ascii:
Small pilot --> delivery / feedback evidence
                       |
                       v
                 Healthy results?
                 + YES --> consider next step
                 + NO ---> hold / fix / retest

steps: Review several sends using bounces, deferrals, complaints, authentication and engagement. A reported 0.38%–1.38% response-to-base ratio alone is not a deliverability test or automatic stop/go threshold.
Continue prioritizing engaged recipients and avoid abrupt spikes or forcing the full list into the early warm-up.
Log each volume change and the evidence behind it; hold, reduce or pause if signals deteriorate.
Advance toward 8,000/day only when results support it. Stage progression and elapsed days alone do not prove inbox readiness.
34.ascii:
Small healthy sends
        |
        v
Evidence review --> gradual increase
        ^                 |
        |                 v
        +-------- monitor next send
Bad signals --> reduce / pause

steps: Refresh suppression and the full-send list immediately before scheduling.
For show invitations, reconcile confirmed Contrast registrants using the working sync or a controlled import; exclude them for this event.
Check remaining daily allowance and other campaign/workflow traffic; account for reset time and the actual recipient count.
If data is stale or capacity is insufficient, reconcile, reduce or reschedule. Do not bypass limits with batching.
35.ascii:
Fresh eligible audience + event exclusions
                     |
                     v
        Compare with remaining capacity
           + fits --> schedule
           + gap ---> reduce / reschedule

steps: Select the refreshed recipient list and tested invitation template in GHL Campaigns.
Choose Batch Schedule: 250 recipients, repeat every 15 minutes, in the intended eight-hour window and timezone.
For exactly 8,000 recipients, use 32 batches. The final batch starts 7 hours 45 minutes after the first; allow processing time. Larger lists require extra batches/time within limits.
Monitor the send, apply stop rules and refresh suppression before any follow-up. Technical readiness, not an event deadline, determines when full volume starts.
37.ascii:
Ready audience --> GHL Batch Schedule
                        |
                        v
250 every 15 min x 32 = 8,000
                        |
                        v
Monitor --> continue OR pause / fix

steps: Open the target GHL sub-account > Settings > Email Services and confirm LC Email is active.
Check account status and live sending allowance, remaining capacity and reset time. Include existing campaign/workflow traffic.
Check agency wallet/credits and ensure funding covers the intended sends; resolve activation or billing errors.
Record these technical settings. LC Email is the selected sending path; no provider-comparison task is required.
03.ascii:
GHL sub-account --> LC Email active
                         |
                         v
            Funded wallet + live sending limit
                         |
                         v
               Configure sending domain

steps: Check the existing DNS records for marketbetter.xyz and mail.marketbetter.xyz; record current values before editing.
In Settings > Email Services > Dedicated Domain and IP, add mail.marketbetter.xyz.
Add the exact provider-generated DNS records at the DNS host. Keep root-domain mailbox routing intact and avoid duplicate SPF records at one hostname.
Wait for DNS propagation and verify the domain in GHL; fix conflicts before continuing.

GHL: Add sending domain
             |
             v
Provider-generated DNS records
             |

DNS provider --> propagation --> GHL verification
